summary: Iron County peak on the Dixie National Forest; the Utah list files it as undocumented, and one unvisited report puts a likely lookout on the summit.

access.note: On national forest land; a Forest Service off-highway vehicle loop carries the peak's name. No source describes access to the summit itself

evidence.supports: peak is filed under unknown/undocumented sites
Utah list row places Horse Valley Peak under Unknown/Undocumented Sites
sites move to lookout lists if regular fire-lookout use is documented
evidence.quote: If evidence or documentation is uncovered showing that any of these were actually used as regular wildland fire lookout sites, they will be moved to the lookout lists.

evidence.supports: a likely lookout on the summit, southeast of Parowan
evidence.quote: Likely on the summit of Horse Valley Peak to the SE of Parowan.

evidence.supports: the list groups sites its author has not visited
Horse Valley Peak Loop is an off-highway vehicle route
loop follows the Smith Canyon road
evidence.quote: The Smith Canyon road travels through lush vegetation and follows the creek-bed several miles.

evidence.supports: off-road section challenging, for experienced riders only
evidence.quote: the OHV section becomes challenging and is recommended for experienced riders only

sources.title: Horse Valley Peak Loop
sources.publisher: Dixie National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

notes_for_editor: No read source describes a lookout structure at this site. The Utah list files it as undocumented; the WillhiteWeb list says a lookout was likely on the summit but its author had not visited. The Forest Service loop page shows an 8,410 ft elevation; not used, because it is not tied to the peak. The loop page does not say whether it reaches the summit. Two web searches used, within budget.
